reflection: Volume-surge factors are the only family with a repeated pattern: they help in 2023 and 2025 and miss in 2022 and 2024, and they help Random Forest more than Logistic Regression. The misses look like noise from single-day volume baselines and from ignoring whether the market rose or fell, so I will test smoother volume baselines and a relative-volume pairing with NVDA. Price-return and gap ideas have mostly been near-copies of existing factors or regime-dependent, so I am moving away from them. Next I will try peer range ratios and Apple's own volume-change dynamics to find signal that is not a restatement of existing volume or volatility features.

lessons.name: qqq_volume_ratio_smooth5d
lessons.lesson: Smoothing the QQQ volume ratio over 5 days removed the daily spikes that had carried the signal, so it lost its small edge and flipped to a negative average gain.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_60d_minus_qqq
lessons.lesson: Using a 60-day volume baseline instead of 20-day helped in 2023 and 2025 but still missed in 2022 and 2024, so the baseline length alone did not fix the direction-blind volume signal.

lessons.name: aapl_drawdown_from_20d_high
lessons.lesson: Its drawdown from the 20-day high was almost a copy of AAPL_close_to_ma20 (similarity 0.91), so it added no new information and its gain was zero.

lessons.name: nvda_volume_surge
lessons.lesson: NVDA's volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 and was an unreliable, mostly Random Forest-only signal that missed badly in 2024, so it needs a smoother or better-conditioned baseline.

lessons.name: aapl_signed_volume_surge
lessons.lesson: Signing Apple's volume surge by its daily direction added little beyond the unsigned surge, because the direction tag did not separate up days from down days consistently across years.

lessons.name: qqq_trend_60d
lessons.lesson: The 60-day QQQ trend was too similar to existing 20-day trend features and failed badly in 2024, so the longer trend window gave no stable edge.

factors.name: nvda_volume_surge_smooth
factors.hypothesis: The raw NVDA volume ratio is noisy day to day and missed in 2022 and 2024; averaging the last 5 days of volume against a 20-day baseline should keep the persistent volume-regime shift and drop single-day spikes.

factors.name: aapl_volume_surge_smooth_minus_qqq
factors.hypothesis: The parent's one-day volume ratios were noisy and missed in 2022 and 2024; using 5-day averaged volumes for both Apple and QQQ should measure a steadier relative volume regime that is not swamped by one-day spikes.

factors.name: peer_range_ratio_msft_nvda
factors.hypothesis: The ratio of MSFT's daily range to NVDA's shows whether the mega-cap tech group is calm or stressed relative to the high-beta AI leader, a market-state signal not yet tested.

factors.name: aapl_volume_change_3d
factors.hypothesis: The three-day change in Apple's raw volume captures whether trading interest is building or fading, which is different from the volume-to-moving-average ratio already tested.

factors.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda
factors.hypothesis: Pairing NVDA's own volume surge with Apple's volume surge relative to NVDA shows whether Apple is attracting more trading than the AI leader, a relative-move angle that complements NVDA's market-level volume signal.

factors.name: aapl_range_surge
factors.hypothesis: Apple's daily range relative to its own 20-day average range measures a volatility surge in Apple itself, which should combine with QQQ's volume surge to show when market-wide activity is spilling into Apple.
